Extending ray-elements

Every ray-elements component is a class built on a few public base classes, and an app can use the same ones. Three levels, from least to most code:

Level What Gets
0 — style tokens, ::part(), Component.extendStyles() looks, custom variants
1 — extend a component class X extends RayButton everything that component does
2 — a new component on a base RayElement, FieldControl, Floating properties, form, ARIA, overlay…

Working examples of levels 1 and 2 (written only against the public API) are in examples/extending, tested in the real webview by tests/extending.test.js.

The contract

Stable (public or protected): everything documented here and in ray-elements.d.ts. Internal: any member of a ray-elements class whose name starts with _ or #. The core keeps its own state in #private fields, so a subclass cannot break it by accident — but do not name your own members with a leading _: component internals (_el, _default…) still use it.

Events

One rule for every component, so nobody has to guess what to listen to:

  • A value changes: change (and input too while it is being edited continuously, as a text field or a slider does). Plain Events that bubble, like the native controls, so forms, React's onChange and Vue's v-model work as usual. They carry no detail: read the new state from the element (value, checked, pressed, files, index…). When something else is worth knowing, it is a property too (ray-file-upload's lastChange: the files the last change added and removed).
  • Anything else: ray-<what>, a CustomEvent from emit() with a typed detail: ray-open, ray-close, ray-select, ray-sort, ray-reject, ray-remove, ray-resize…
  • A container stops the change events of its own parts and fires its own (ray-toggle-group stops its toggles'); a listener on a container still sees the changes of the controls slotted in it, so check e.target.

RayElement (core.js)

Member
static properties { name: { type, reflect, attribute, default } } → accessors, observed attributes, reflection
static styles / static template constructable sheets / shadow markup (cloned per instance)
static delegatesFocus focus goes to the first focusable inside
static extendStyles(...sheets) adds CSS to the component and its subclasses, live instances included
update(changed) protected: render; changed maps changed properties to their previous values
commitProperty(name, value) protected: set a property without reflecting it (state the user changed)
hasValue(name) protected: the property has its own value (not the default)
requestUpdate() schedule update
emit(type, detail, { cancelable }) bubbling, composed CustomEvent
$(selector) shadowRoot.querySelector
paintIcons(root) protected: fill [data-ray-icon="name"] placeholders from the icon registry

Call super.connectedCallback() / super.disconnectedCallback() when you override them.

FormControl and FieldControl (form.js)

FormControl = RayElement + ElementInternals: form, validity, checkValidity(), reportValidity(), effectivelyDisabled (own attribute or a disabled <fieldset>), forward(event) (re-dispatch a non-composed event such as change from the host).

FieldControl = a FormControl around one native control with id="control" in its template:

Member
static fieldProperties spread into properties: name, label, description, error, required, disabled, size, radius, variant
fieldTemplate(controlHtml, { sections }) label + description + box + error markup around your control
fieldStyles, boxStyles, sizeStyles, radiusStyles the shared look
control the native control
wire() protected hook: attach listeners once
syncField() protected: label, description, error, required, disabled and their ARIA; call it from update
syncValidity() protected: mirror the control's validity into the form

You still call this.internals.setFormValue(…) and implement formResetCallback(). See examples/extending/components/color-field.

Floating (floating.js)

A trigger (slot trigger by default) and a [popover] panel (.panel in your template) in the top layer, placed with flip and shift.

Member
static popoverMode "manual" (default: Floating closes it — Escape, outside press, one open at a time — and animates the exit) or "auto" (the browser's light dismiss, no exit animation)
static lightDismiss false for panels that must not close on Escape/outside press (tooltips)
exitKeyframes() protected hook: the keyframes the panel leaves with
static haspopup / popupKind() aria-haspopup of the trigger (null: none)
static triggerSlot selector of the trigger slot
open, placement, offset, show(), hide(), toggle()
wireTrigger(trigger) protected hook: your trigger listeners
anchorRect(), placeOptions() protected: what to anchor to, extra place() options
toggled(open) protected hook: after opening/closing
focusWasInside, justClosed() focus return, light-dismiss vs. trigger click

See examples/extending/components/hover-card.

Helpers

css, define, uid, applyColor(el, color) + variantStyles (the filled/light/outline/subtle/default variants on [data-variant]), loaderStyles, srOnlyStyles, place(), autoUpdate(), tabbables(), focusFirst(), setIcons() / getIcon(), configure().

Motion (core/motion.js): play(el, keyframes, { speed, ease }) runs an animation with the duration/easing tokens and resolves when it ends — at once with reduced motion, a zero duration or a hidden page — so a component can hide an element only after its exit (await play(...).finished; el.hidden = true). collapseOut(el) folds an element away; POP_OUT is the exit of floating panels. RayDialog (and so RayDrawer) has an exitKeyframes() hook too. Light dismiss (core/dismiss.js): dismissable({ panel, owner, trigger, close }) gives a manual popover Escape and outside-press closing, nested panels included. Shortcuts (core/hotkey.js): matchesHotkey(e, "mod+k"), formatHotkey("mod+k") (⌘K / Ctrl K).

Level 0: styling without a new component

import { RayButton, css } from "@raylang/elements";

// A custom variant: <ray-button variant="brand">
RayButton.extendStyles(css`
  [data-variant="brand"] { background: #7c3aed; color: white; }
  [data-interactive]:not([data-disabled])[data-variant="brand"]:hover { background: #6d28d9; }
`);

From a plain stylesheet, ::part() works too: ray-button[variant="brand"]::part(button) { … }.

App-wide defaults for properties left unset:

import { configure } from "@raylang/elements";
configure({ defaults: { "ray-button": { variant: "light", size: "md" } } });

Level 1: extend a component

import { RayButton, css, define } from "@raylang/elements";

export class AppSaveButton extends RayButton {
  static properties = { ...RayButton.properties, dirty: { type: Boolean, reflect: true } };
  static styles = [...RayButton.styles, css`:host([dirty]) { … }`];
  update(changed) {
    super.update(changed);   // everything ray-button does
    // …your additions
  }
}
define("app-save-button", AppSaveButton);

Types, manifest and React/Vue wrappers for your components

Describe each component in a component.toml (same format as ray-elements's, any category, extends naming its parent class) next to its JS, then:

tools/run.sh wrap --components ../my-app/src/components --out ../my-app/src/ray-wrappers

It writes index.js (registers your components, re-exports ray-elements), index.d.ts (classes extending ray-elements's, HTMLElementTagNameMap), react.js/react.d.ts and vue.js/vue.d.ts (made with createComponent from @raylang/react / @raylang/vue, inheriting the parent's props: an extends = "FieldControl" component gets label, required… typed) and custom-elements.json. To wrap a component by hand instead:

import { createComponent } from "@raylang/react";
export const AppSaveButton = createComponent("app-save-button", {
  properties: ["dirty", "variant"], events: { onRaySelect: "ray-select" },
});
